Tawney, Eileen Power, and Douglass North. Further approaches include Polanyi, The Great Transformation (1944); Gerschenkron, Economic Backwardness in Historical Perspective (1962 collection); de Vries’s industrious-revolution article (1994); Pomeranz, The Great Divergence (2000). E. A. Wrigley: People, Cities and Wealth (1987); Continuity, Chance and Change (1988).

strand.title: Corporate capitalism, finance and public power
strand.focus: White’s Railroaded asks how debt-financed corporations, public subsidies and political markets could enrich insiders despite repeated corporate failure. This is an inquiry into the institutional operation of American capitalism, distinct from the feudal transition, industrial growth and slavery controversies grouped elsewhere here.
